issues.legal_issue: A land-ceiling rule that treats a Hindu undivided family as one landholding unit for ceiling purposes is protected from constitutional challenges to property and equality rights when it forms part of agrarian reform.
material_facts: The land was held by a Hindu undivided family, with the land recorded in the name of its head.
The family members argued that each was entitled to retain a separate ceiling area from the family holding.
The challenged rule treated the family holding as the land of the family head for the purposes of the land-reform scheme and prevented descendants from claiming separate ceiling areas.
The scheme limited holdings, acquired surplus land for distribution, and preserved family members’ rights in the retained area and their entitlement to compensation for surplus land.
issues.conclusion: The rule formed part of agrarian reform and was protected by Article 31-A from challenges under Articles 14, 19 and 31. The challenge failed and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A protects laws providing for the acquisition of an estate or rights in it, or the extinguishment or modification of such rights, from challenges under Articles 14, 19 and 31 when the law concerns agrarian reform. Ranjit Singh v. State of Punjab held that land ceilings and related measures can constitute agrarian reform. K. K. Kochuni v. State of Madras confined Article 31-A’s protection to measures directed to agrarian reform. Pritam Singh v. State of Punjab upheld the protection of a rule disregarding certain land transfers for surplus-land purposes. The challenged rule prevented a family from multiplying its ceiling area through separate claims by descendants, while leaving their other family-property rights and compensation rights unaffected. The Court also noted that a challenge to Article 31-A itself was unavailable in light of I. C. Golak Nath v. State of Punjab.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_ceiling: A person challenges a rule governing the maximum landholding and acquisition of surplus land on constitutional-rights grounds.
predicates.joint_family_treated_as_one_unit_for_cei: The rule treats land held by a joint family as one holding for calculating the family’s permissible area.
predicates.rule_aimed_at_surplus_land_distribution: The rule is part of a scheme intended to acquire surplus land and make it available for distribution.
predicates.other_family_property_rights_preserved: The rule leaves family members’ other rights in family property and their entitlement to compensation for acquired surplus land unaffected.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a land-ceiling rule that counts a joint family as one holding to support surplus-land distribution while preserving its members’ other family-property rights, the rule is protected from the constitutional-rights challenge.
